tools.name: memory_search
tools.title: Search memories
tools.description: Search long-term memories collected across all past chats. Hybrid semantic + keyword + entity-graph retrieval. Returns the current version of each fact with provenance. Use it before answering anything about the user's life, preferences, history, people or projects.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language.

chat_id.description: Only memories first observed in this chat.

kinds.description: fact, preference, event, plan, relationship, opinion, identity, task, other

since.description: ISO date lower bound on the memory's date.

until.description: ISO date upper bound on the memory's date.

include_superseded.description: Also return the history of facts that were later updated.

tools.name: memory_context
tools.title: Memory context block
tools.description: Return a compact block of the memories most relevant to a query, ready to paste into a prompt or read before replying. Empty string when nothing relevant is stored.

tools.name: memory_add_message
tools.title: Record a chat message
tools.description: Store one message of a conversation so the background worker (a local Qwen model) can turn it into memories and relationships. Returns immediately; extraction happens asynchronously. Use the same chat_id for all messages of one conversation.

speaker.description: Who said it: the person's name, or 'user' / 'assistant'.

sent_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the message (defaults to now).

message_id.description: Optional stable id for idempotent re-sends.

tools.name: memory_remember
tools.title: Remember a fact now
tools.description: Store an explicit memory immediately (no extraction step), e.g. when the user says 'remember that ...'. The text should be one self-contained third-person sentence.

subject.description: Who/what the memory is about (defaults to 'user').

when.description: Date the memory is about (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY).

tools.name: memory_profile
tools.title: Profile of a person or entity
tools.description: Everything currently known about a subject: memories grouped by kind and the entity's relations.

tools.name: memory_related
tools.title: Related memories
tools.description: Memories linked to a given memory id (supersedes, contradicts, related, elaborates) and its history.

tools.name: memory_entities
tools.title: Entity graph
tools.description: Top entities by mentions, or the typed relations of one entity (1-hop neighbourhood).

entity.description: Entity name; omit for the top list.

tools.name: memory_forget
tools.title: Forget a memory
tools.description: Retract a memory (and the relations grounded in it) at the user's request. Keeps an audit entry.

tools.name: memory_status
tools.title: Memory system status
tools.description: Counts, worker/queue state, token savings and the five-axis grade of the memory system.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Hi! I'm Ali. I just moved from Baku to Berlin last month for a nursing job at Charité, and I'm trying to get organised.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Welcome to Berlin, Ali! Congratulations on the new role at Charité. What would you like to organise first?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Mostly my training plan. I signed up for the Berlin half marathon on 5 April and I've never run more than 12 km. Also my cat Luna needs a vet, she's 3 and due for her shots.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Five weeks is tight but doable. Let's build a plan: three runs a week, one long run growing from 12 km to 18 km. For Luna, most vets in Prenzlauer Berg take walk-ins on Saturdays.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Quick one: I'm vegetarian and allergic to peanuts. Can you suggest a high-protein dinner I can cook in 20 minutes? My sister Leyla is visiting from Baku tonight.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Try a chickpea and spinach curry with paneer: 20 minutes, about 30 g protein per serving, no nuts.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Leyla hates spinach, she's been like that since we were kids. I'll swap it for peas. She's staying until Sunday.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Peas work well. Enjoy the evening with Leyla!

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I did it! Finished the half marathon yesterday in 2:04. My colleague Jonas from the cardiology ward ran it too and beat me by ten minutes, so now we're planning the Hamburg marathon in September.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Huge congratulations on 2:04! A September marathon gives you about 22 weeks, which is a healthy build-up.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Also, I moved flats: I'm now in Kreuzberg, not Prenzlauer Berg. The old place was too loud. Luna approves of the balcony.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Noted, Kreuzberg it is. Glad Luna likes the balcony.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Rough week. I'm switching from the night shift to days from June, and I'm thinking about starting a part-time master's in public health at TU Berlin in October. Jonas says it's a lot with marathon training.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Day shifts will make a study schedule far more predictable. If you apply, the TU Berlin deadline for October intake is usually mid-July.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Good to know. Remind me later: my mother's birthday is 22 June and I want to send flowers to Baku.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: I'll keep that in mind: flowers to Baku for 22 June.

messages.speaker: Ali
messages.text: I moved to Berlin in March and my cat Luna is 3 years old.
